name: Minoan palatial
description: Palace societies on Crete (Knossos, Phaistos, Malia) using Linear A, an undeciphered script. Their religion is known from images and objects, not readable texts.

name: Mycenaean
description: Late Bronze Age mainland palaces (Mycenae, Pylos, Thebes) write an early form of Greek in Linear B. The tablets name several later Greek gods.

name: Collapse & Early Iron Age
description: Palaces are destroyed, writing disappears for centuries, and population falls. Sometimes called a 'Dark Age', though sites like Lefkandi show wealth and contacts.

name: Archaic
description: The alphabet, the city-state, Panhellenic sanctuaries, and the first surviving Greek poetry: Homer and Hesiod fix the myths in writing.

name: Classical
description: From the Persian Wars to Alexander's death: Athenian drama, the Parthenon, and the first prose historians.

name: Hellenistic
description: Alexander's successor kingdoms spread Greek culture from Egypt to Afghanistan; Greek and local gods are combined in new cults.

name: Roman
description: Rome develops alongside the Greek world, then rules it. Romans equate their gods with Greek ones (interpretatio) and retell Greek myth in Latin. Overlaps the Greek periods on purpose.

name: Late Antique transformation
description: Christianity becomes the imperial religion; public sacrifice is banned and temples close or are converted, while myth survives in literature, art and education.
